How Things Are Going Now

Northrop Grumman's core defense franchises continue to benefit from structural demand tied to the modernization of the U.S. nuclear triad and national security space architectures. Over the trailing four quarters, quarterly revenue advanced from $9,881M in Q1 2026 to $10,876M in Q2 and $11,122.0M in Q3 (+6.7% YoY), establishing a real-time annualized run-rate of $44,488.0M. Segment operating margin reached 12.1% in the latest quarter, driven by solid volume in Aeronautics Systems (+14% YoY to $3.58B) and Defense Systems (+12% YoY to $2.31B), partially offset by moderate EAC friction in Space Systems. Net order intake was robust at $16.4B in Q3, representing a book-to-bill of 1.48x and expanding total backlog to a company record $109.6B.

This $109.6B backlog provides approximately 2.5 years of forward revenue visibility across critical national security programs. Aeronautics growth is supported by sustained F-35 center fuselage manufacturing, B-21 Raider LRIP lot execution, and B-2 fleet sustainment, while Defense Systems reflects the expansion of the Sentinel (LGM-35A) engineering and manufacturing development contract. Year-to-date operating cash flow reached inflection in Q3 with $2,116M generated, allowing management to raise full-year MTM-adjusted EPS guidance to $29.35–$29.75 and confirm full-year free cash flow guidance of $3.1B–$3.5B.

Capital deployment is explicitly oriented toward capacity expansion and internal manufacturing readiness. Management has paused share repurchases ($0M executed in Q2 and Q3 2026) to fund a multi-year $2.5B facility expansion program, with capital expenditures projected to reach ~$2.1B in 2027 to scale solid rocket motor tooling and classified aeronautics facilities. While the share repurchase pause limits near-term share count reduction, it preserves balance sheet liquidity and strengthens the company's sole-source position across franchise defense programs.
